=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- File: scripts/workflow_retro.py
  Line or code reference: lines 581-584 (fetch_merged_pull_requests failure path) and line 669-671 (has_activity computation)
  Problem: When fetch_merged_pull_requests fails, merged_prs becomes [] and merged_pr_count is 0. If total_runs is also 0, has_activity evaluates to False and the retro is skipped entirely. A transient GitHub API failure for merged PRs therefore suppresses the retro even when merged-PR activity is unknown.
  Why it fails at runtime: A weekly run with zero CI runs but some merged PRs will fetch those PRs via the fail-open GitHub API call. If that call fails (rate limit, network, auth), merged_prs goes to [], has_activity becomes false, and the retro step is skipped — no tracker comment, no Telegram alert, no human-visible signal that merged PR data may have been missed. The existing fail-open pattern for this repo treats unknown data as "do not skip" (e.g. memory failures still allow the retro to proceed via total_runs; a non-2xx from the merged-PR API does not make merged_pr_count zero, it just means the count is stale). This one data-source failure path silently kills the retro.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- File: scripts/security_audit.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 225-262 (scope resolution block)
  Problem: When LAST_AUDITED_SHA is empty (first run, no tracker issue yet) but HEAD_SHA is non-empty, the outer else at line 260 overwrites AUDIT_SCOPE_REASON from its initial "no last-audited commit recorded on the tracker" to "SECURITY_AUDIT_INCREMENTAL is disabled". This reason is misleading — incremental was never evaluated; there was simply no baseline SHA to diff against.
  Why it fails at runtime: The audit still runs in full-scope mode and the Codex call / tracker comment proceed normally, so this is an observability-only defect. Operators reading the run log or tracker comment would see the wrong reason ("incremental is disabled") which can mask the real situation (no prior audit recorded).
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
